So I tried a moly based and a Teflon based dry lube inside my magazines at matches over the weekend. Ground is very sandy soil that can migrate into pistols from magazines very easily. Pistols run best lightly oiled to factory spec. Any magazine that touched the ground is broken down and wiped out with a rag. Previous to this I have had at least one malfunction a day. This weekend zero malfunctions.

I recommend the Teflon based dry lube, it repels oil that may get on it. The moly would get wet if oil got on it. I don't know if it helped keep sand from sticking or just decreased friction but it seemed to help.

I tore apart, cleaned dry, and then sprayed a Ciener type device with a spray on dry Moly lube. It worked really well, but sometime when shooting with a suppressor the humidity comes back into the action and started to gum it up a little. I never thought about how Moly is affected by anything wet; I was just thinking about burned powder residue and unburned powder inhibiting the action from working.

What product did you use? I wouldn't mind tearing it down again and spraying it with dry lube again.

Realistically, the Moly I used was adequate. I fired several hundred rounds over a few weekends without any major problems other than ammo, but I'm always looking to improve. I've read that several Walther P-22 owners use a spray on dry lube with great success, but you have to completely degrease the firearm first.

I use normal gun oil in the pistol for lubrication. Cleaning is break free clp spray for the bore and large areas, clp liquid for sensitive areas, then Birchwood Casey gun scrubber over everything. I was using hoppes 9 black oil. I just got some breakthrough battle born lube, not for a change in oil but for the needle applicator to put less on.

In the magazines I degreased and cleaned with Birchwood Casey gun scrubber. Then sprayed the inside of the body with blaster dry lube with Teflon. After it dries assemble the magazine without wiping out or anything.
